texts.1ki.14.10: therefore, behold me! bringing misfortune against the house of Jeroboam, and I will cut off the meanest pertaining to Jeroboam, whether shut up or left at large, in Israel,—and will consume after the house of Jeroboam, as one consumeth dung, till it be all gone:
texts.1ki.14.11: Him that dieth of Jeroboam in the city, shall, the dogs, eat, and, him that dieth in the field, shall, the birds of heaven, eat,—For, Yahweh, hath spoken.
texts.1ki.14.12: Thou, therefore, arise, go to thine own house,—as thy feet are entering the city, the young man shall die.
texts.1ki.14.13: Then shall all Israel lament for him, and bury him, for, this one, pertaining to Jeroboam, shall reach a burying-place,—because there hath been found in him something good toward Yahweh, God of Israel, in the house of Jeroboam.
texts.1ki.14.14: Therefore will Yahweh raise up for himself a king over Israel, who will cut off the house of Jeroboam, this day, but why, even now?
texts.1ki.14.15: Therefore will Yahweh smite Israel, as a reed shaketh in water, and will root out Israel, from off this goodly soil, which he gave unto their fathers, and will scatter them beyond the River (Euphrates),—because they have made their Sacred Stems, provoking Yahweh to anger:
texts.1ki.14.16: That he may deliver up Israel,—on account of the sin of Jeroboam, which he committed, and which he caused, Israel, to commit.
texts.1ki.14.17: Then arose the wife of Jeroboam, and went her way and entered Tirzah,—as, she, was coming into the entrance hall, the young man died.
texts.1ki.14.18: And, when they buried him, all Israel lamented him,—according to the word of Yahweh, which he spake through his servant Ahijah the prophet.
texts.1ki.14.19: Now, the rest of the story of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, behold them! written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
texts.1ki.14.20: And, the days which Jeroboam reigned, were twenty-two years,—and he slept with his fathers, and, Nadab his son, reigned, in his stead.
texts.1ki.14.21: And, Rehoboam, son of Solomon, reigned in Judah,—forty-one years old, was Rehoboam when he began to reign, and seventeen years, reigned he in Jerusalem, the city which Yahweh had chosen to put his Name there, out of all the tribes of Israel, and, his mother’s name, was Naamah, the Ammonitess.
texts.1ki.14.22: And Judah did the thing that was wicked in the eyes of Yahweh,—and provoked him to jealousy, above all that their fathers had done, with their sins which they committed.
texts.1ki.14.23: And, they also, built for themselves high places and pillars, and Sacred Stems,—upon every high hill, and under every green tree.
texts.1ki.14.24: Moreover also, there were, male devotees, in the land,—they did according to all the abominable practices of the nations, which Yahweh dispossessed from before the sons of Israel.
texts.1ki.14.25: And it came to pass, in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, that Shishak king of Egypt, came up against Jerusalem;
texts.1ki.14.26: and took away the treasures of the house of Yahweh, and the treasures of the house of the king, yea, the whole, took he away,—and took away all the bucklers of gold, which, Solomon, had made.
texts.1ki.14.27: So King Rehoboam made, in their stead, bucklers of bronze,—and committed them unto the hand of the captains of the runners, who kept guard at the entrance of the house of the king.
texts.1ki.14.28: And so it was, whensoever the king went into the house of Yahweh, the runners bare them, and then brought them back into the chamber of the runners.
texts.1ki.14.29: Now, the rest of the story of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are, they, not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
texts.1ki.14.30: And there was, war, between Rehoboam and Jeroboam, continually.
texts.1ki.14.31: So then Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and, the name of his mother, was Naamah the Ammonitess,—and, Abijah his son, reigned, in his stead.
texts.1ki.15.1: Now, in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, began Abijah to reign over Judah.
texts.1ki.15.2: Three years, reigned he in Jerusalem,—and, the name of his mother, was Maachah, daughter of Abishalom.
texts.1ki.15.3: And he walked in all the sins of his father which he had done before him,—and his heart was not blameless with Yahweh his God, like the heart of David his father.
texts.1ki.15.4: But, for the sake of David, did Yahweh his God give him a lamp, in Jerusalem,—by raising up a son of his after him, and by suffering Jerusalem to stand;
texts.1ki.15.5: because David did that which was right in the eyes of Yahweh,—and turned not aside from anything that he commanded him, all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
texts.1ki.15.6: And there was, war, between Rehoboam and Jeroboam, all the days of his life.
texts.1ki.15.7: Now, the rest of the story of Abijah and all that he did, are, they, not written in the book of Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? And there was, war, between Abijah and Jeroboam.
texts.1ki.15.8: So then Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David,—and, Asa his son, reigned, in his stead.
texts.1ki.15.9: Now, in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, began Asa to reign as king of Judah;
texts.1ki.15.10: and, forty-one years, reigned he in Jerusalem,—and, the name of his mother, was Maachah, daughter of Abishalom.
texts.1ki.15.11: And Asa did that which was right in the eyes of Yahweh,—like David his father;
texts.1ki.15.12: and he put away the male devotees out of the land,—and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.
texts.1ki.15.13: Moreover also, even Maachah his mother, he removed from being queen, because she had made a monstrous thing to the Sacred Stem,—and Asa cut down her monstrous thing and burned it in the Kidron ravine.
texts.1ki.15.14: But, the high places, removed he not,—nevertheless, the heart of Asa, was blameless with Yahweh, all his days.
texts.1ki.15.15: And he brought in the hallowed things of his father, and his own hallowed things, into the house of Yahweh,—silver and gold, and vessels.
texts.1ki.15.16: And there was, war, between Asa and Baasha king of Israel, all their days.
texts.1ki.15.17: And Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah, and built Ramah,—so as not to suffer any one to come out or go in unto Asa king of Judah.
texts.1ki.15.18: So Asa took all the silver and the gold, that were left in the treasuries of the house of Yahweh, and the treasures of the house of the king, and delivered them into the hand of his servants,—and King Asa sent them unto Ben-hadad, son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, king of Syria, who dwelt in Damascus, saying:
texts.1ki.15.19: [Let there be a] covenant between me and thee, [as] between my father and thy father: Lo! I have sent thee a gift, silver and gold, Come break thy covenant with Baasha, king of Israel, that he may go up from against me.
texts.1ki.15.20: So Ben-hadad hearkened unto King Asa, and sent the generals of the forces which he had, against the cities of Israel, and smote Iyyohn [Ijon], and Dan, and Abel-beth-maacah,—and all Chinneroth, against all the land of Naphtali.
texts.1ki.15.21: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard thereof, he left off building Ramah,—and returned to Tirzah.
texts.1ki.15.22: And, King Asa, published it unto all Judah, none was exempted, so they carried away the stones of Ramah, and the beams thereof, wherewith Baasha had built,—and King Asa built therewith Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah.
texts.1ki.15.23: Now, the rest of all the story of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did and the cities which he built, are, they, not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? Howbeit, in the time of his old age, he was diseased in his feet.
texts.1ki.15.24: So then Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers, in the city of David his father,—and, Jehoshaphat his son, reigned, in his stead.
texts.1ki.15.25: Now, Nadab son of Jeroboam, began to reign over Israel, in the second year of Asa king of Judah,—and he reigned over Israel, two years.
texts.1ki.15.26: And he did the thing that was wicked in the eyes of Yahweh,—and walked in the way of his father, and in his sin, wherewith he caused, Israel, to sin.
texts.1ki.15.27: And Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him, and Baasha smote him in Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines,—Nadab and all Israel being in siege against Gibbethon.
texts.1ki.15.28: And Baasha slew him, in the third year of Asa king of Judah,—and reigned in his stead.
texts.1ki.15.29: And it came to pass, when he became king, that he smote all the house of Jeroboam, he left not remaining any breathing thing pertaining to Jeroboam, until he had destroyed him,—according to the word of Yahweh, which he spake by the hand of his servant Ahijah the Shilonite:
texts.1ki.15.30: for the sins of Jeroboam which he committed, and which he caused, Israel, to commit,—by his provocation wherewith he provoked to anger Yahweh God of Israel.
texts.1ki.15.31: Now, the rest of the story of Nadab, and all that he did, are, they, not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
texts.1ki.15.32: And there was, war, between Asa and Baasha king of Israel, all their days.
texts.1ki.15.33: In the third year of Asa king of Judah, began Baasha, son of Ahijah, to reign over all Israel, in Tirzah, [and he reigned] twenty-four years.
texts.1ki.15.34: And he did that which was wicked in the eyes of Yahweh,—and walked in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin wherewith he caused, Israel, to sin.
texts.1ki.16.1: Then came the word of Yahweh unto Jehu
texts.1ki.16.2: son of Hanani, against Baasha, saying: Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust, and gave thee to be leader over my people Israel,—and yet thou hast walked in the way of Jeroboam, and caused, my people Israel, to sin, provoking me to anger with their sins,
texts.1ki.16.3: Behold me! consuming after Baasha, and after his house,—and I will deliver up thy house, like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat:
texts.1ki.16.4: Him that dieth of Baasha in the city, shall, the dogs, eat, and, him that dieth of his in the field, shall, the birds of heaven, eat.
texts.1ki.16.5: Now, the rest of the story of Baasha, and what he did, and his might, are, they, not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
texts.1ki.16.6: So Baasha slept with his fathers, and was buried in Tirzah,—and, Elah his son, reigned, in his stead.
texts.1ki.16.7: Moreover also, through Jehu son of Hanani the prophet, the word of Yahweh, came against Baasha and against his house, even because of all the wickedness that he had done in the eyes of Yahweh, provoking him to anger with the work of his hands, becoming like the house of Jeroboam,—notwithstanding that he smote him.
texts.1ki.16.8: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, began Elah son of Baasha to reign over Israel, in Tirzah, [and he reigned] two years.
texts.1ki.16.9: Then conspired against him his servant Zimri, captain of half the chariots,—as he was in Tirzah drinking himself drunk, in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah.
texts.1ki.16.10: And Zimri went in, and smote him and slew him, in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah,—and reigned in his stead.
texts.1ki.16.11: And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he smote all the house of Baasha, he left him not even the meanest,—neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.
texts.1ki.16.12: Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha,—according to the word of Yahweh which he spake unto Baasha, through Jehu the prophet;
texts.1ki.16.13: as to all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son,—wherewith they sinned, and wherewith they caused, Israel, to sin, provoking to anger Yahweh God of Israel, with their vanities.
texts.1ki.16.14: Now, the rest of the story of Elah, and all that he did, are, they, not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
texts.1ki.16.15: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, did Zimri reign, seven days in Tirzah,—but, the people, were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistine.
texts.1ki.16.16: When therefore the people who were encamped, heard say, Zimri hath conspired, moreover also, he hath smitten the king, all Israel made Omri, general of the army, king over Israel, on that day, in the camp.
texts.1ki.16.17: So Omri, and all Israel with him, went up from Gibbethon,—and laid siege against Tirzah.
texts.1ki.16.18: And it came to pass, when Zimri saw that the city was captured, that he entered into the citadel of the house of the king,—and burned over him the house of the king, with fire, and died:
texts.1ki.16.19: because of his sins which he committed by doing the thing that was wicked in the eyes of Yahweh,—by walking in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin which he committed, by causing, Israel, to sin.
texts.1ki.16.20: Now, the rest of the story of Zimri, and his conspiracy wherein he conspired, are, they, not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
texts.1ki.16.21: Then, were the people of Israel divided,—half the people, were following Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and, half, following Omri.
texts.1ki.16.22: But, the people that followed Omri, prevailed against, the people that followed Tibni son of Ginath; so that, Tibni, died, and, Omri, reigned.
texts.1ki.16.23: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, began Omri to reign over Israel [and he reigned] twelve years: in Tirzah, reigned he six years.
texts.1ki.16.24: And he bought the hill Samaria, of Shemer, for two talents of silver,—and built on the hill, and called the name of the city which he built, after the name of Shemer lord of the hill—Samaria.
texts.1ki.16.25: And Omri did the thing that was wicked in the eyes of Yahweh,—and did more wickedly than all who were before him;
texts.1ki.16.26: yea he walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and in his sin wherewith he caused, Israel, to sin,—provoking to anger Yahweh, God of Israel, with their vanities.
texts.1ki.16.27: Now, the rest of the story of Omri, what he did, and his might that he shewed, are, they, not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
texts.1ki.16.28: So Omri slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria,—and, Ahab his son, reigned, in his stead.
texts.1ki.16.29: Now, Ahab son of Omri, began to reign over Israel, in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah,—and Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel, in Samaria, twenty-two years.
texts.1ki.16.30: And Ahab son of Omri did the thing that was wicked in the eyes of Yahweh,—and did more wickedly than all that were before him.
texts.1ki.16.31: And it come to pass, as though it had been too light a thing that he should walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, that he took to wife Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and bowed down to him.
texts.1ki.16.32: And he reared an altar unto Baal,—in the house of Baal, which he built in Samaria.
texts.1ki.16.33: And Ahab made the Sacred Stem,—and Ahab did yet more to provoke to anger Yahweh God of Israel than all the kings of Israel who were before him.
texts.1ki.16.34: In his days, did Hiel the Bethelite build Jericho,—At the price of Abiram his firstborn, he laid its foundation, and, at the price of Segub his youngest, he set up its doors, according to the word of Yahweh which he spake through Joshua son of Nun.
texts.1ki.17.1: Then said Elijah the Tishbite, of Tishbe in Gilead, unto Ahab, By the life of Yahweh, God of Israel, before whom I stand, there shall not, these two years, be either dew or rain,—save at the bidding of my word.
texts.1ki.17.2: Then came the word of Yahweh unto him, saying:
texts.1ki.17.3: Get thee hence, and turn thee eastward,—and hide thyself in the ravine of Cherith, which faceth the Jordan;
texts.1ki.17.4: and it shall be that, of the torrent, shalt thou drink,—and, the ravens, have I commanded to sustain thee, there.
texts.1ki.17.5: So he went and did, according to the word of Yahweh,—yea he went and dwelt in the ravine of Cherith, which faceth the Jordan.
texts.1ki.17.6: And, the ravens, used to bring him bread and flesh, in the morning, and bread and flesh, in the evening,—and, of the torrent, used he to drink.
texts.1ki.17.7: But it came to pass, at the end of [certain] days, that the torrent dried up,—because there had been no rain in the land.
texts.1ki.17.8: Then came the word of Yahweh unto him, saying—
texts.1ki.17.9: Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon, and dwell there,—Lo! I have commanded, there, a widow woman, to sustain thee.
texts.1ki.17.10: So he arose and went to Zarephath, and, when he came to the entrance of the city, lo! there, a widow woman gathering sticks,—and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
texts.1ki.17.11: And, as she went to fetch it, he called to her and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread, in thy hand.
texts.1ki.17.12: And she said—By the life of Yahweh, thy God, verily I have not a cake, only a handful of meal in the jar, and a little oil in the cruse,—and lo! I have been gathering a couple of sticks, so I shall go in and make it ready for me and for my son, that we may eat it—and die!
texts.1ki.17.13: And Elijah said unto her—Do not fear, go in—make ready according to thy word,—howbeit, make me thereof a little cake, first, and bring it out to me, and, for thyself and thy son, make ready, afterwards.
texts.1ki.17.14: For, thus, saith Yahweh, God of Israel, The jar of meal, shall not waste, and, the cruse of oil, shall not fail,—until the day that Yahweh giveth rain upon the face of the ground.
texts.1ki.17.15: So she went and made ready, according to the word of Elijah,—and did eat, she, and he, and her house, [certain] days:
texts.1ki.17.16: The jar of meal, did not waste,—and, the cruse of oil, did not fail,—according to the word of Yahweh, which he spake through Elijah.
texts.1ki.17.17: And it came to pass, after these things, that the son of the woman, owner of the house, fell sick,—yea it came to pass that his sickness was very severe, until no, breath, was left in him.
texts.1ki.17.18: Then said she unto Elijah, What have I in common with thee, O man of God? Hast thou come unto me, to call to remembrance mine iniquity, and to cause the death of my son?
texts.1ki.17.19: And he said unto her—Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him unto the upper room, where, he, was staying, and laid him upon his own bed.
texts.1ki.17.20: Then cried he unto Yahweh, and said,—O Yahweh, my God! Even upon the widow with whom I am sojourning, hast thou brought misfortune by causing the death of her son?
texts.1ki.17.21: And he stretched himself out upon the boy, three times, and cried unto Yahweh, and said,—O Yahweh, my God! Let the life of this boy, I pray thee, come again within him.
texts.1ki.17.22: And Yahweh hearkened unto the voice of Elijah,—and the life of the boy came again within him, and he lived.
texts.1ki.17.23: Then Elijah took the boy, and carried him down out of the upper room, into the house, and gave him to his mother,—and Elijah said, See! thy son liveth.
texts.1ki.17.24: And the woman said unto Elijah, Now, then I know, that, a man of God, thou art,—and that, the word of Yahweh, is in thy mouth, of a truth.
texts.1ki.18.1: And it came to pass, after many days, that, the word of Yahweh, came unto Elijah, in the third year, saying,—Go, shew thyself unto Ahab, that I may send rain upon the face of the ground.
texts.1ki.18.2: And Elijah went, to show himself unto Ahab. Now, the famine, was severe in Samaria.
texts.1ki.18.3: And Ahab had called for Obadiah, who was over his house. Now, Obadiah, was one who revered Yahweh, exceedingly.
texts.1ki.18.4: And so it came to pass, when Jezebel was cutting off the prophets of Yahweh, that Obadiah took a hundred prophets, and hid them by fifties in caves, and sustained them, with bread and water.
texts.1ki.18.5: So then Ahab said unto Obadiah, Go, and let us pass throughout the land, unto all the fountains of water, and unto all the ravines, peradventure we may find grass, and save alive horse and mule, and not have more of the beasts cut off.
texts.1ki.18.6: So they divided to them the land, to pass through it,—Ahab, went one way, by himself, and, Obadiah, went another way, by himself.
texts.1ki.18.7: And so it was, as Obadiah was on the road, that lo! Elijah, met him,—and he recognised him, and fell upon his face, and said—Now art, thou, my lord Elijah?
texts.1ki.18.8: And he said to him—I, am! Go, say to thy lord: Here, is, Elijah!
texts.1ki.18.9: And he said—How have I sinned,—that, thou, art delivering thy servant into the hand of Ahab, to put me to death?
texts.1ki.18.10: By the life of Yahweh thy God, there is no nation or kingdom, whither my lord hath not sent to seek thee, and, when they have said—Nay! he hath taken an oath of the kingdom or the nation, that no one could find thee;
texts.1ki.18.11: and, now, thou, art saying,—Go say to thy lord, Here, is, Elijah;
texts.1ki.18.12: so shall it come to pass, as soon as, I, go from thee, that, the spirit of Yahweh, shall carry thee away—whither I know not, and so, when I go in to tell Ahab, and he cannot find thee, then will he slay me,—and yet, thy servant, hath revered Yahweh, from my youth.
texts.1ki.18.13: Was it not told my lord, what I did when Jezebel was slaying the prophets of Yahweh,—how I hid, of the prophets of Yahweh, a hundred men—by fifties—in caves, and sustained them with bread and water?
texts.1ki.18.14: and yet, now, thou, art saying, Go, tell thy lord—Here, is, Elijah; and so he will slay me!
texts.1ki.18.15: Then said Elijah—By the life of Yahweh of hosts, before whom I stand, to-day, will I show myself unto him.
texts.1ki.18.16: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab, and told him,—and, Ahab, went to meet, Elijah.
texts.1ki.18.17: And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Now, art, thou, troubling Israel?
texts.1ki.18.18: And he said—I have not troubled Israel, but, thou and the house of thy father,—in that ye have forsaken the commandments of Yahweh, and followed Baal.
texts.1ki.18.19: Now, therefore, send, gather unto me all Israel, unto Mount Carmel,—and the prophets of Baal, four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the Sacred Stem, four hundred, who do eat at the table of Jezebel.
texts.1ki.18.20: So Ahab sent among all the sons of Israel,—and gathered the prophets unto Mount Carmel.
texts.1ki.18.21: And Elijah drew near unto all the people, and said—How long are ye limping on the two divided opinions? If, Yahweh, be GOD, follow, him, but, if, Baal, follow, him. But the people answered him, not a word.
texts.1ki.18.22: Then said Elijah unto the people—I, am left, Yahweh’s, only, prophet,—but, the prophets of Baal, are four hundred and fifty men.
texts.1ki.18.23: Let there be given us, therefore, two bullocks, and let them choose for themselves one bullock, and cut it in pieces, and lay it upon the wood, but, fire, shall they not put,—then, I, will make ready the other bullock, and place upon the wood, but, fire, will I not put.
texts.1ki.18.24: Then shall ye call on the name of your god, and, I, will call on the name of Yahweh, and it shall be, the God that respondeth by fire, he, is GOD. And all the people responded—Well spoken!
texts.1ki.18.25: Then said Elijah to the prophets of Baal—Choose for yourselves one bullock, and make ye ready, first, for, ye, are many,—and call ye on the name of your god, but, fire, shall ye not put.
texts.1ki.18.26: So they took the bullock which was given them, and made ready, and called on the name of Baal—from the morning even until the noon, saying—O Baal! answer us. But them was no voice, nor any that answered. And they leaped about by the altar which had been made.
texts.1ki.18.27: And it came to pass, at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said—Cry with a loud voice, for, a god, he is, either he hath, a meditation, or an occasion to retire, or he hath, a journey,—peradventure, he, sleepeth, and must be awaked.
texts.1ki.18.28: And they cried, with a loud voice, and cut themselves, after their custom, with swords, and with lances,—until the blood gushed out upon them.
texts.1ki.18.29: And so it was, when noon was passed, that although they prophesied until the offering up of the evening gift, yet was there no voice nor any that answered, nor any that hearkened.
texts.1ki.18.30: Then said Elijah unto all the people: Draw near unto, me. And all the people drew near unto, him. Then repaired he the broken-down altar of Yahweh; yea Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob,—
texts.1ki.18.31: unto whom the word of Yahweh came, saying—Israel, shall be thy name;
texts.1ki.18.32: and built, with the stones, an altar, in the name of Yahweh,—and he made a trench, as large as would contain two measures of seed, round about the altar;
texts.1ki.18.33: and he put in order the wood,—and cut in pieces the bullock, and laid upon the wood. Then said he—Fill four pitchers with water, and pour out upon the ascending-sacrifice, and upon the wood. And they did so.
texts.1ki.18.34: And he said—Do it the second time. And they did it the second time. And he said—Do it the third time. And they did it the third time.
texts.1ki.18.35: And the water ran round about the altar,—moreover also, the trench, filled he with water.
texts.1ki.18.36: And it came to pass, at the time of the offering of the gift, that Elijah the prophet drew near, and said, O Yahweh, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel! To-day, let it be known—That, thou, art God in Israel, and that, I, am thy servant,—and that, by thy word, have I done all these things.
texts.1ki.18.37: Answer me, O Yahweh! answer me, That this people may know, that, thou—Yahweh, art GOD,—so shalt, thou thyself, have turned their heart back again.
texts.1ki.18.38: Then fell fire from Yahweh, and consumed the ascending-sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust,—even the water that was in the trench, it licked up.
texts.1ki.18.39: And, when all the people saw it, they fell upon their faces,—and said, Yahweh, he, is GOD, Yahweh, he, is GOD.
texts.1ki.18.40: And Elijah said unto them—Seize ye the prophets of Baal—let not, a man, of them escape. So they seized them. And Elijah took them down unto the ravine of Kishon, and slaughtered them there.
texts.1ki.18.41: Then said Elijah unto Ahab, Go up, eat and drink,—for there is a sound of a downpour of rain.
texts.1ki.18.42: So Ahab went up, to eat and to drink,—but, Elijah, went up to the top of Carmel, and bowed himself to the earth, and put his face between his knees.
texts.1ki.18.43: Then said he unto his young man—Go up, I pray thee, and look about in the direction of the sea. So he went up, and looked about, and said—There is, nothing whatever. Then said he—Go again, seven times.
texts.1ki.18.44: And it came to pass, at the seventh time, that he said, Lo! a little cloud, like a man’s hand coming up from the sea. Then he said—Go up, say unto Ahab—Harness, and get thee down, lest the rain shut thee in.
texts.1ki.18.45: And it came to pass, meanwhile, that, the heavens, had enshrouded themselves with clouds and wind, and there came a great rain, and Ahab rode, and went to Jezreel;
texts.1ki.18.46: but, the hand of Yahweh, came upon Elijah, so he girded his loins,—and ran before Ahab, until thou enterest Jezreel.
texts.1ki.19.1: And Ahab told Jezebel, all that Elijah had done,—and withal, how he had slain all the prophets with the sword.
texts.1ki.19.2: Then sent Jezebel a messenger unto Elijah, saying,—So, let the gods do, and, so, let them add, if, by this time to-morrow, I make not thy life as the life of one of them.
texts.1ki.19.3: And, when he saw [that], he arose, and went for his life, and came to Beer-sheba, which belongeth to Judah,—and left his servant there.
texts.1ki.19.4: But, he himself, went into the wilderness a day’s journey, and came and sat down under a certain shrub,—and asked for his life, that he might die, and said—Enough, now, O Yahweh! take away my life, for, no better, am, I, than, my fathers.
texts.1ki.19.5: And, as he lay, and slept, under a certain shrub, lo! a messenger, touching him, who said to him—Rise, eat.
texts.1ki.19.6: So he looked about, and lo! at his head, a cake baked on hot stones, and a cruse of water,—and he did eat and drink, and then went back and lay down.
texts.1ki.19.7: And the messenger of Yahweh came again a second time, and touched him, and said—Rise, eat,—because, too much for thee, is the journey.
texts.1ki.19.8: So he arose, and did eat and drink,—and journeyed, in the strength of that eating, forty days and forty nights, as far as the mountain of God—Horeb.
texts.1ki.19.9: And he entered, there, into a cave, and lodged there,—and lo! the word of Yahweh [came] unto him, and said to him, What doest thou here, Elijah?
texts.1ki.19.10: And he said—Very jealous, have I been, for Yahweh, God of hosts, because the sons of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thine altars, have they thrown down, thy prophets, also have they slain with the sword,—and, I alone, am left, and they have sought my life, to take it.
texts.1ki.19.11: And he said—Go forth to-morrow, and stand in the mountain, before Yahweh. And lo! Yahweh, passing by, and a great and strong wind—rending the mountains, and breaking in pieces the crags, before Yahweh, Not, in the wind, was, Yahweh,—And, after the wind, an, earthquake, Not, in the earthquake, was, Yahweh;
texts.1ki.19.12: And, after the earthquake, a, fire, Not, in the fire, was, Yahweh,—And, after the fire, the voice of a gentle whisper.
texts.1ki.19.13: And it came to pass, when Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went forth, and stood at the entrance of the cave,—and lo! unto him, a voice; and it said—What doest thou here, Elijah?
texts.1ki.19.14: And he said—Very jealous, have I been, for Yahweh, God of hosts, because the sons of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thine altars, have they thrown down, thy prophets also, have they slain with the sword,—and, I alone, am left, and they rove sought my life, to take it.
texts.1ki.19.15: And Yahweh said unto him, Go, return to thy way, towards the wilderness of Damascus,—and, when thou enterest, then shalt thou anoint Hazael to be king over Syria;
texts.1ki.19.16: And, Jehu son of Minshi, shalt thou anoint to be king over Israel,—and, Elisha son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah, shalt thou anoint to be prophet in thy stead:
texts.1ki.19.17: Then shall it come to pass, that—him that escapeth the sword of Hazael, shall, Jehu, slay,—and, him that escapeth the sword of Jehu, shall, Elisha, slay;
texts.1ki.19.18: Yet will I leave remaining in Israel, seven thousand,—all knees which have not bowed to Baal, and all mouths which have not kissed to him.
texts.1ki.19.19: So he departed from thence, and found Elisha son of Shaphat, as he was plowing, with twelve yoke of oxen before him, he being with the twelfth,—so Elijah crossed over unto him, and cast his mantle towards him;
texts.1ki.19.20: and he left the oxen, and ran after Elijah, and said—Let me, I pray thee, kiss my father and my mother, that I may follow thee. And he said unto him,—Go, turn back, for what have I done to thee?
texts.1ki.19.21: So he turned back from following him, and took the yoke of oxen, and sacrificed them, and, with the implements of the oxen, boiled their flesh, and gave unto the people, and they did eat,—then he arose, and followed Elijah, and ministered unto him.
texts.1ki.20.1: Now, Ben-hadad, king of Syria, had gathered together all his forces, and, thirty-two kings, were with him, and horses and chariots,—then came he up, and laid siege to Samaria, and made war against it.
texts.1ki.20.2: And he sent messengers unto Ahab king of Israel, into the city, and said to him,—Thus, saith Ben-hadad,
texts.1ki.20.3: Thy silver and thy gold, are, mine, and, thy wives and thy sons, the goodliest, are, mine.
texts.1ki.20.4: Then responded the king of Israel, and said, According to thy word, my lord O king! thine, am I, and all that I have.
texts.1ki.20.5: And the messengers came back again, and said, Thus, speaketh Ben-hadad, saying,—Because I sent unto thee, saying, Thy silver and thy gold and thy wives and thy sons, to me, shalt thou give,
texts.1ki.20.6: Therefore, about this time to-morrow, will I send my servants unto thee, and they shall search thy house, and the houses of thy servants,—and it shall be, that, all the delight of thine eyes, shall they put in their hand, and take away.
texts.1ki.20.7: Then called the king of Israel, for all the elders of the land, and said—Mark, I pray you, and see, how this man is seeking, mischief,—for he had sent unto me, for my wives, and for my sons, and for my silver, and for my gold, and I refused him not.
texts.1ki.20.8: And all the elders and all the people said unto him,—Do not thou hearken, neither do thou consent.
texts.1ki.20.9: So he said unto the messengers of Ben-hadad—Say ye to my lord the king,—All that thou didst send for, to thy servant at the first, will I do, but, this thing, I cannot do. And the messengers departed, and took him back word.
texts.1ki.20.10: Then Ben-hadad sent unto him and said,—So, let the gods do to me, and, so, let them add,—if the dust of Samaria suffice by handfuls, for all the people who are at my feet.
texts.1ki.20.11: And the king of Israel responded and said: Tell him,—Let not, him that girdeth, boast himself like him, that looseneth.
texts.1ki.20.12: And it came to pass, when he heard this message, as, he, was drinking, he and the kings in the pavilions, that he said unto his servants—Make ready! So they made ready, against the city.
texts.1ki.20.13: And lo! a certain prophet, drew near unto Ahab king of Israel, and said,—Thus, saith Yahweh, Hast thou seen all this great multitude? Behold me! delivering it into thy hand, to-day, so shalt thou know that, I, am, Yahweh.
texts.1ki.20.14: And Ahab said—By whom? And he said—Thus, saith Yahweh, By the young men of the princes of the provinces. Then said he—Who shall begin the war? And he said—Thou!
texts.1ki.20.15: Then numbered he the young men of the princes of the provinces, and they were found to be, two hundred and thirty-two,—and, after them, he numbered all the people all the sons of Israel, seven thousand.
texts.1ki.20.16: And they went forth at noon. Now, Ben-hadad, was drinking himself drunk, in the pavilions, he and the thirty-two kings helping him.
texts.1ki.20.17: Then went forth the young men of the princes of the provinces, first,—and, when Ben-hadad sent, they told him, saying—Men, have come forth, out of Samaria.
texts.1ki.20.18: And he said—If, peaceably, they have come, take them alive,—or, if, fighting, they have come, alive, take ye them.
texts.1ki.20.19: Now, when, these, had come forth out of the city, even the young men of the princes of the provinces,—with the force which was following them,
texts.1ki.20.20: then smote they every one his man, and the Syrians fled, and Israel pursued them,—but Ben-hadad king of Syria escaped on horse, with horsemen.
texts.1ki.20.21: And the king of Israel went forth, and took the horses and the chariots,—and he went on smiting the Syrians, with a great smiting.
texts.1ki.20.22: Then drew near the prophet, unto the king of Israel, and said unto him—Go strengthen thyself, and mark and see, what thou wilt do,—for, at the return of the year, is, the king of Syria, coming up against thee.
texts.1ki.20.23: And, the servants of the king of Syria, said unto him,—Gods of the mountains, are their gods, for this cause, prevailed they against us,—but, only let us fight with them in the plain, and verily we shall prevail against them.
texts.1ki.20.24: But, this thing, do,—set aside the kings, every man out of his place, and put governors in their stead;
texts.1ki.20.25: and, thou, must number thee a force, like the force which thou hast lost, both horse for horse and chariot for chariot, and, if we fight with them in the plain, verily we shall prevail against them. And he hearkened unto their voice, and did so.
texts.1ki.20.26: And so it came to pass at the return of the year, that Ben-hadad numbered the Syrians,—and came up to Aphek, to fight with Israel;
texts.1ki.20.27: and, the sons of Israel, were numbered, and provisioned, and went to meet them,—and the sons of Israel encamped before them like two little flocks of goats, whereas, the Syrians, filled the land.
texts.1ki.20.28: Then approached the man of God, and spake unto the king of Israel, and said—Thus, saith Yahweh—Because the Syrians have said—A god of the mountains, is Yahweh, but, not a god of the vales, is he, therefore will I deliver all this great multitude, into thy hand, so shalt thou know, that, I, am Yahweh.
texts.1ki.20.29: So they encamped, these, over against, those, seven days,—and it came to pass, on the seventh day, that the battle was joined, and the sons of Israel smote the Syrians, a hundred thousand footmen, in one day.
texts.1ki.20.30: And they who were left fled to Aphek, into the city, and the wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand men who were left,—and, Ben-hadad, fled, and came into the city, into a chamber within a chamber.
texts.1ki.20.31: And his servants said unto him, Lo! we pray thee, we have heard, of the kings of the house of Israel, that, kings known for lovingkindness, they are. Let us, we pray thee, put sackcloth upon our loins, and ropes about our head, and let us go forth unto the king of Israel, peradventure he will save alive thy soul.
texts.1ki.20.32: So they girded sackcloth upon their loins, and [put] ropes about their heads, and came in unto the king of Israel, and said, Thy servant, Ben-hadad, saith,—Let my soul live, I pray thee. And he said,—Is he yet alive? My brother, he is.
texts.1ki.20.33: Now, the men, could divine, so they hastened to let him confirm the word of his own accord, and they said,—Thy brother, is Ben-hadad! He said therefore,—Go fetch him. So Ben-hadad came forth unto him, and he made him come up unto him on his chariot.
texts.1ki.20.34: And he said unto him—The cities which my father took from thy father, will I restore, and, bazaars, shalt thou make thee in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria. So then, I, with this covenant, will let thee go. So he solemnised with him a covenant, and let him go.
texts.1ki.20.35: And, a certain man of the sons of the prophets, said unto his neighbour, by the word of Yahweh—Smite me, I pray thee. But the man refused to smite him.
texts.1ki.20.36: So he said to him—Because thou hast not hearkened unto the voice of Yahweh, lo! when thou art departing from me, there shall smite thee a lion. And when he departed from beside him, a lion found him, and smote him.
texts.1ki.20.37: Then found he another man, and said,—Smite me, I pray thee. So the man smote him—kept on smiting and wounding.
texts.1ki.20.38: Then the prophet departed, and waited for the king, by the way,—and disguised himself with his turban over his eyes.
texts.1ki.20.39: And so it was, when, the king, was passing, he, cried out unto the king,—and said—Thy servant, went out in the midst of the battle, and lo! a man, turned aside and brought unto me a man, and said—Keep this man, if he be, missing, then shall, thy life, go for, his life, or, a talent of silver, shalt thou weigh out.
texts.1ki.20.40: And so it was, as thy servant was busy here and there, that, he, was gone. And the king of Israel said unto him—Such, is thy judgment, thou thyself, hast decided it.
texts.1ki.20.41: Then hastened he, and removed the turban from over his eyes,—and the king of Israel knew him, that, of the prophets, was, he.
texts.1ki.20.42: And he said unto him—Thus, saith Yahweh, Because thou hast let go the man whom I had devoted, out of thy hand, therefore shall, thy life, be instead of, his life, and, thy people, instead of, his people.
texts.1ki.20.43: And the king of Israel departed unto his house, sullen and disturbed,—and entered Samaria.
texts.1ki.21.1: And it came to pass, after these things, that Naboth the Jezreelite had, a vineyard, which was in Jezreel,—hard by the palace of Ahab, king of Samaria.
texts.1ki.21.2: Ahab, therefore, spake unto Naboth, saying—Come! give me thy vineyard, that I may have it for a garden of herbs, for, the same, is near by my house, and let me give thee, instead thereof, a vineyard better than it,—if it be good in thine eyes, I will give thee silver to the value of this.
texts.1ki.21.3: And Naboth said unto Ahab,—Far be it from me, of Yahweh! that I should give up the inheritance of my fathers, unto thee!
texts.1ki.21.4: So Ahab came into his house, sullen and disturbed, because of the word which Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken unto him, that he should have said, I will not give thee the inheritance of my fathers. So he laid him down upon his bed, and turned away his face, and did eat no food.
texts.1ki.21.5: Then came unto him Jezebel his wife,—and said unto him—Why is it, that thy spirit is sullen, that thou art, not eating food?
texts.1ki.21.6: And he said unto her—Because I spake unto Naboth, the Jezreelite, and said unto him—Come! give me thy vineyard for silver, or, if thou wouldst prefer, I will give thee a vineyard, in its stead; and he said—I will not give thee my vineyard.
texts.1ki.21.7: Then Jezebel his wife said unto him: Art, thou, still, going to carry on the kingdom over Israel? Rise! eat food, and let thy heart be merry, I, will give thee the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite!
texts.1ki.21.8: So she wrote letters, in the name of Ahab, and sealed them with his signet-ring,—and sent the letters unto the elders, and unto the nobles who were in his city, dwelling with Naboth.
texts.1ki.21.9: Now she wrote in the letters, saying,—Proclaim ye a fast, and cause Naboth to sit at the head of the people;
texts.1ki.21.10: then let two reckless men take their seats before him, that they may bear witness against him, saying, Thou hast reviled God and king! then shall ye carry him forth and stone him, that he die.
texts.1ki.21.11: So the men of his city, the elders and the nobles who dwelt in his city, did just as Jezebel had sent unto them,—as it was written in the letters which she had sent unto them:
texts.1ki.21.12: they proclaimed a fast,—and caused Naboth to sit at the head of the people.
texts.1ki.21.13: Then came in the two reckless men, and sat before him, and the men bare witness against him, even against Naboth, before the people, saying, Naboth hath reviled God and king! So they carried him forth, outside the city, and stoned him with stones, that he died.
texts.1ki.21.14: Then sent they unto Jezebel, saying,—Naboth is stoned and is dead.
texts.1ki.21.15: And it came to pass, when Jezebel heard that Naboth was stoned and was dead, that Jezebel said unto Ahab—Rise! take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give thee for silver, for Naboth is not alive, but dead!
texts.1ki.21.16: And it came to pass, when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, that Ahab arose, to go down unto the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession thereof.
texts.1ki.21.17: Then came the word of Yahweh unto Elijah the Tishbite, saying:
texts.1ki.21.18: Arise! go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria,—lo! he is in the vineyard of Naboth, whither he hath gone down, to take possession thereof.
texts.1ki.21.19: Then shalt thou speak unto him, saying—Thus, saith Yahweh, Hast thou committed murder, and also taken possession? Then shalt thou speak unto him, saying: Thus, saith Yahweh, In the place where the dogs have lapped up the blood of Naboth, shall the dogs lap up thy blood, even thine.
texts.1ki.21.20: Then said Ahab unto Elijah, Hast thou found me, O mine enemy? And he said: I have found [thee]! Because thou hast sold thyself to do the thing that is wicked in the eyes of Yahweh,
texts.1ki.21.21: Behold me! [saith he] bringing in upon thee, calamity, and I will consume after thee,—and cut off of Ahab, even the meanest, whether shut up or left at large in Israel;
texts.1ki.21.22: and will deliver up thy house—Like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah,—for the provocation wherewith thou hast provoked, and caused, Israel, to sin.
texts.1ki.21.23: Moreover also, concerning Jezebel, hath Yahweh spoken, saying,—The dogs, shall eat Jezebel, in the town-land of Jezreel:
texts.1ki.21.24: Him that dieth, of Ahab, in the city, shall, the dogs, eat,—and, him that dieth in the field, shall, the birds of heaven, eat.
texts.1ki.21.25: But indeed, there was none like Ahab, who sold himself to do the thing that was wicked in the eyes of Yahweh,—whom Jezebel his wife goaded on;
texts.1ki.21.26: so that he did very abominably, in going after the manufactured gods,—according to all which the Amorites had done, whom Yahweh dispossessed from before the sons of Israel.
texts.1ki.21.27: And it came to pass, when Ahab heard these words, that he rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his flesh, and fasted,—and lay in sackcloth, and went softly.
texts.1ki.21.28: Then came the word of Yahweh unto Elijah the Tishbite, saying:
texts.1ki.21.29: Hast thou seen that Ahab hath humbled himself, before me? Because he hath humbled himself before me, I will not bring in the calamity in his days, In the days of his son, will I bring in the calamity upon his house.
texts.1ki.22.1: And there continued three years without war between Syria and Israel.
texts.1ki.22.2: But it came to pass, in the third year, that Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down unto the king of Israel.
texts.1ki.22.3: And the king of Israel said unto his servants, Know ye that, ours, is Ramoth-gilead,—yet, we, are too idle to take it out of the hand of the king of Syria?
texts.1ki.22.4: And he said unto Jehoshaphat, Wilt thou go with me to make war upon Ramoth-gilead?
texts.1ki.22.5: And Jehoshaphat said unto the king of Israel, I am as thou art, my people are us thy people, my horses as thy horses.
texts.1ki.22.6: Then said Jehoshaphat unto the king of Israel,—Seek, I pray thee, at once, the word of Yahweh. So the king of Israel gathered together the prophets, about four hundred men, and said unto them—Shall I go against Ramoth-gilead, to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said—Go up, that the Lord may deliver it into the hand of the king.
texts.1ki.22.7: Then said Jehoshaphat, Is there not here a prophet of Yahweh, besides,—that we may seek, from him?
texts.1ki.22.8: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, Besides, is a certain man, by whom we might seek Yahweh, but, I, hate him, for he is never moved to prophesy concerning me anything good, only evil, Micaiah, son of Imlah. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.
texts.1ki.22.9: Then the king of Israel called a certain courtier,—and said, Hasten Micaiah son of Imlah.
texts.1ki.22.10: Now, the king of Israel, and Jehoshaphat king of Judah, were sitting—each man upon his throne, having put on robes, in a level place, at the entrance of the gate of Samaria,—and, all the prophets, were being moved to prophesy before them;
texts.1ki.22.11: when Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself horns of iron,—and said—Thus, saith Yahweh,—With these, shalt thou push down the Syrians, until thou hast consumed them.
texts.1ki.22.12: And, all the prophets, were being moved to prophesy, in like manner, saying,—Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and thou shalt prosper, and Yahweh will deliver it, into the hand of the king.
texts.1ki.22.13: Now, the messenger who went to call Micaiah, spake unto him, saying, Behold, I pray thee, the words of the prophets, with one mouth, are good, as touching the king, let thy word, I pray thee, be as the word of one of them, so wilt thou speak that which is good.
texts.1ki.22.14: And Micaiah said,—By the life of Yahweh, what Yahweh saith unto me, that, will I, speak.
texts.1ki.22.15: So he came unto the king, and the king said unto him, Micaiah, shall we go against Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall we forbear? And he said unto him—Go up and prosper, and Yahweh will deliver it into the hand of the king.
texts.1ki.22.16: And the king said unto him, How many times must, I, adjure thee,—that thou speak unto me nothing but truth, in the name of Yahweh?
texts.1ki.22.17: And he said—I saw all Israel, scattered among the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd,—so Yahweh said, These have, no masters, let them return every man unto his own house, in peace.
texts.1ki.22.18: Then said the king of Israel, unto Jehoshaphat,—Did I not say unto thee, He will not be moved to prophesy concerning me anything good, only calamity.
texts.1ki.22.19: Then he said, Therefore, hear thou the word of Yahweh,—I saw Yahweh, sitting upon his throne, and all the host of the heavens, standing by him, on his right hand, and on his left.
texts.1ki.22.20: And Yahweh said, Who will persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall, at Ramoth-gilead? And, one, said in this manner, and, another, said in that manner.
texts.1ki.22.21: Then came forth a spirit, and stood before Yahweh, and said—I, will persuade him.
texts.1ki.22.22: And Yahweh said unto him—Wherewith? And he said—I will go forth, and become a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his prophets,—So he said,—Thou mayest persuade, yea and prevail, go forth, and do so.
texts.1ki.22.23: Now, therefore, lo! Yahweh hath suffered a spirit of falsehood to be put into the mouth of all these thy prophets. But, Yahweh himself, hath spoken concerning thee, calamity.
texts.1ki.22.24: Then drew near Zedekiah, son of Chenaanah, and smote Micaiah on the cheek,—and said—Where then passed the Spirit of Yahweh, from me, to speak unto thee?
texts.1ki.22.25: Then said Micaiah, Lo! thou art about to see, on that day,—when thou enterest a chamber within a chamber, to hide thyself.
texts.1ki.22.26: And the king of Israel said, Take Micaiah, and carry him back unto Amon captain of the city,—and unto Joash son of the king;
texts.1ki.22.27: and thou shalt say—Thus, saith the king, Put this man into the prison,—and let him eat the bread of oppression, with the water of oppression, until I enter in peace.
texts.1ki.22.28: Then said Micaiah, If thou, return, in peace, Yahweh hath not spoken by me. And he said, Hear, ye peoples, all of you!
texts.1ki.22.29: So the king of Israel went up, with Jehoshaphat king of Judah, unto Ramoth-gilead.
texts.1ki.22.30: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat—I am about to disguise myself, and enter into the battle, thou, therefore, put on thy robes. So the king of Israel disguised himself, and entered into the battle.
texts.1ki.22.31: Now, the king of Syria, had commanded the captains of chariots which he had, thirty and two, saying, Ye shall not fight with small or great,—save with the king of Israel alone.
texts.1ki.22.32: And it came to pass, when the chariot-captains saw Jehoshaphat, that, they, said: Surely it is, the king of Israel! But, when they turned aside against him to fight, Jehoshaphat cried out.
texts.1ki.22.33: And it came to pass, when the chariot-captains saw that it was, not the king of Israel, that they turned back, from pursuing him.
texts.1ki.22.34: But, a certain man, drawing a bow in his innocence, smote the king of Israel, between the shoulder-joints and the coat of mail,—wherefore he said to his charioteer—Turn thy hand, and convey me out of the host, for I am sore wounded.
texts.1ki.22.35: But the battle increased that day, and, the king, was propped up in the chariot, before the Syrians,—and died in the evening, and so the blood of the wound ran out into the hollow of the chariot.
texts.1ki.22.36: And a loud cry went through the host, at the going in of the sun, saying—Every man to his own city! and every man to his own land!
texts.1ki.22.37: So the king died, and was brought into Samaria,—and they buried the king, in Samaria.
texts.1ki.22.38: And, when the chariot was washed out at the pool of Samaria, the dogs lapped up his blood, also, the harlots, bathed [there],—according to the word of Yahweh which he had spoken.
texts.1ki.22.39: Now, the rest of the story of Ahab, and all that he did, and the house of ivory that he built, and all the cities that he built, are, they, not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
texts.1ki.22.40: So Ahab slept with his fathers,—and, Ahaziah his son, reigned, in his stead.
texts.1ki.22.41: Now, Jehoshaphat son of Asa, began to reign over Judah,—in the fourth year of Ahab, king of Israel.
texts.1ki.22.42: Jehoshaphat, was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and, twenty-five years, reigned he in Jerusalem,—and, the name of his mother, was Azubah, daughter of Shilhi.
texts.1ki.22.43: And he walked in all the way of Asa his father, he turned not aside therefrom,—doing that which was right in the eyes of Yahweh: nevertheless, the high places, were not taken away,—still were the people offering sacrifices and burning incense in the high places.
texts.1ki.22.44: And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
texts.1ki.22.45: Now, the rest of the story of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he shewed, and how he warred, are, they, not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
texts.1ki.22.46: Moreover, the rest of the male devotees who remained in the days of Asa his father, he consumed out of the land.
texts.1ki.22.47: And, king, was there none in Edom, a prefect, was king.
texts.1ki.22.48: Jehoshaphat, made ships of Tarshish, to go to Ophir, for gold; but they went not,—for ships had been broken to pieces in Ezion-geber.
texts.1ki.22.49: Then, said Ahaziah son of Ahab, unto Jehoshaphat, Let, my servants, go with, thy servants, in the ships,—but Jehoshaphat did not consent.
texts.1ki.22.50: So Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers, in the city of David his father,—and, Jehoram his son, reigned, in his stead.
texts.1ki.22.51: Ahaziah son of Ahab, began to reign over Israel, in Samaria, in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah,—and reigned over Israel, two years.
texts.1ki.22.52: And he did the thing that was wicked in the eyes of Yahweh,—and went in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused, Israel, to sin.
texts.1ki.22.53: Yea he served Baal, and bowed down to him,—and provoked to anger Yahweh, God of Israel, according to all that his father had done.

texts.1ki.1.1: El rey David era ya viejo y entrado en años; y por más que lo cubrían con ropas, no podía calentarse.
texts.1ki.1.2: Por lo tanto, sus siervos le dijeron: «Búsquese una joven virgen para mi señor el rey, para que esté en presencia del rey y lo abrigue, y duerma en su seno; así mi señor el rey entrará en calor».
texts.1ki.1.3: Buscaron, pues, a una joven hermosa por todos los confines de Israel, y hallaron a Abisag la sunamita, y la llevaron ante el rey.
texts.1ki.1.4: La joven era muy hermosa, y se puso al servicio del rey para cuidarlo, mas el rey no la conoció íntimamente.
texts.1ki.1.5: Entonces Adonías, hijo de Haggit, se enalteció diciendo: «Yo seré el rey». Y se hizo de carros y jinetes, y de cincuenta hombres que corrieran delante de él.
texts.1ki.1.6: Su padre nunca le había recriminado nada ni le había dicho: «¿Por qué haces esto?». Además, era un hombre muy apuesto y había nacido después de Absalón.
texts.1ki.1.7: Se puso de acuerdo con Joab hijo de Sarvia y con el sacerdote Abiatar, los cuales seguían a Adonías y le prestaban su apoyo.
texts.1ki.1.8: Pero ni el sacerdote Sadoc, ni Benaía hijo de Joiada, ni el profeta Natán, ni Simei, ni Rei, ni los valientes de David estaban con Adonías.
texts.1ki.1.9: Adonías sacrificó ovejas, bueyes y animales cebados junto a la piedra de Zohelet, que está cerca de En-Rogel; e invitó a todos sus hermanos, los hijos del rey, y a todos los hombres de Judá, siervos del rey;
texts.1ki.1.10: pero no invitó al profeta Natán, ni a Benaía, ni a los valientes, ni a su hermano Salomón.
texts.1ki.1.11: Entonces Natán habló a Betsabé, madre de Salomón, diciendo: “¿No has oído que Adonías hijo de Haggit se ha proclamado rey, sin que nuestro señor David lo sepa?
texts.1ki.1.12: Ven, pues, ahora, y permite que te dé un consejo para que salves tu vida y la de tu hijo Salomón.
texts.1ki.1.13: Ve, entra al rey David y dile: ‘¿No jurasteis vos, mi señor el rey, a vuestra sierva, diciendo: «Ciertamente tu hijo Salomón reinará después de mí y se sentará en mi trono»? ¿Por qué, pues, reina Adonías?’.
texts.1ki.1.14: Mira, mientras aún estés hablando allí con el rey, yo entraré tras de ti y confirmaré tus palabras”.
texts.1ki.1.15: Betsabé entró en la cámara del rey. El rey era ya muy anciano, y Abisag la sunamita servía al rey.
texts.1ki.1.16: Betsabé se inclinó y rindió homenaje al rey. El rey preguntó: «¿Qué deseas?».
texts.1ki.1.17: Ella respondió: “Señor mío, vos jurasteis por Yahvé vuestro Dios a vuestra sierva: ‘Ciertamente tu hijo Salomón reinará después de mí y se sentará en mi trono’.
texts.1ki.1.18: Y ved que ahora Adonías reina, y vos, mi señor el rey, no lo sabéis.
texts.1ki.1.19: Ha sacrificado bueyes, animales cebados y ovejas en abundancia, y ha invitado a todos los hijos del rey, al sacerdote Abiatar y a Joab, general del ejército; pero no ha invitado a Salomón, vuestro siervo.
texts.1ki.1.20: En vos, mi señor el rey, están puestos los ojos de todo Israel, para que les declaréis quién ha de sentarse en el trono de mi señor el rey después de él.
texts.1ki.1.21: De lo contrario, sucederá que cuando mi señor el rey duerma con sus padres, yo y mi hijo Salomón seremos tenidos por culpables”.
texts.1ki.1.22: Mientras ella aún hablaba con el rey, entró el profeta Natán.
texts.1ki.1.23: Avisaron al rey, diciendo: «He aquí el profeta Natán». Al entrar ante el rey, se postró rostro en tierra.
texts.1ki.1.24: Y Natán dijo: “Rey, señor mío, ¿habéis dicho vos: ‘Adonías reinará después de mí y se sentará en mi trono’?
texts.1ki.1.25: Porque hoy ha bajado y ha sacrificado bueyes, animales cebados y ovejas en abundancia, y ha invitado a todos los hijos del rey, a los capitanes del ejército y al sacerdote Abiatar; y ved que están comiendo y bebiendo delante de él, y dicen: ‘¡Viva el rey Adonías!’.
texts.1ki.1.26: Pero a mí, vuestro siervo, ni al sacerdote Sadoc, ni a Benaía hijo de Joiada, ni a vuestro siervo Salomón, nos ha invitado.
texts.1ki.1.27: ¿Ha emanado esta orden de mi señor el rey, sin haber declarado a vuestros siervos quién se sentaría en el trono de mi señor el rey después de él?”.
texts.1ki.1.28: El rey David respondió: «Llamadme a Betsabé». Ella entró a la presencia del rey y se puso en pie ante él.
texts.1ki.1.29: Entonces el rey juró diciendo: “Vive Yahvé, que ha redimido mi alma de toda angustia,
texts.1ki.1.30: que tal como os juré por Yahvé, Dios de Israel, diciendo: ‘Ciertamente tu hijo Salomón reinará después de mí y se sentará en mi trono en mi lugar’, así lo haré hoy mismo”.
texts.1ki.1.31: Entonces Betsabé se inclinó rostro en tierra, rindió homenaje al rey y dijo: «¡Viva mi señor el rey David para siempre!».
texts.1ki.1.32: El rey David ordenó: «Llamadme al sacerdote Sadoc, al profeta Natán y a Benaía hijo de Joiada». Ellos se presentaron ante el rey.
texts.1ki.1.33: Y el rey les dijo: “Llevad con vosotros a los siervos de vuestro señor, haced montar a mi hijo Salomón en mi propia mula y llevadlo a Gihón.
texts.1ki.1.34: Que el sacerdote Sadoc y el profeta Natán lo unjan allí como rey sobre Israel. Tocad la trompeta y decid: ‘¡Viva el rey Salomón!’.
texts.1ki.1.35: Subid tras él, y vendrá y se sentará en mi trono, pues él reinará en mi lugar; porque a él lo he designado para que sea príncipe sobre Israel y sobre Judá”.
texts.1ki.1.36: Benaía hijo de Joiada respondió al rey: «¡Amén! Así lo diga Yahvé, el Dios de mi señor el rey.
texts.1ki.1.37: Como Yahvé ha estado con mi señor el rey, así esté con Salomón, y haga su trono más grande que el trono de mi señor el rey David».
texts.1ki.1.38: Bajaron, pues, el sacerdote Sadoc, el profeta Natán, Benaía hijo de Joiada, y los cereteos y los peleteos, e hicieron montar a Salomón en la mula del rey David y lo llevaron a Gihón.
texts.1ki.1.39: El sacerdote Sadoc tomó el cuerno de aceite del Tabernáculo y ungió a Salomón. Tocaron la trompeta y todo el pueblo exclamó: «¡Viva el rey Salomón!».
texts.1ki.1.40: Todo el pueblo subió tras él; y la gente tocaba flautas y se regocijaba con gran alegría, de tal modo que la tierra se estremecía con el estruendo.
texts.1ki.1.41: Lo oyeron Adonías y todos los invitados que estaban con él, cuando ya habían acabado de comer. Al oír Joab el sonido de la trompeta, preguntó: «¿A qué viene ese alboroto en la ciudad?».
texts.1ki.1.42: Mientras aún hablaba, llegó Jonatán, hijo del sacerdote Abiatar, a quien Adonías dijo: «Entra, porque eres hombre de valía y traes buenas noticias».
texts.1ki.1.43: Jonatán respondió a Adonías: “Al contrario; nuestro señor el rey David ha hecho rey a Salomón.
texts.1ki.1.44: El rey ha enviado con él al sacerdote Sadoc, al profeta Natán, a Benaía hijo de Joiada, y a los cereteos y los peleteos, y lo han montado en la mula del rey.
texts.1ki.1.45: El sacerdote Sadoc y el profeta Natán lo han ungido rey en Gihón; de allí han subido con gran júbilo, y la ciudad está alborotada. Ese es el estruendo que habéis oído.
texts.1ki.1.46: Además, Salomón ya se ha sentado en el trono del reino.
texts.1ki.1.47: Y también los siervos del rey han ido a felicitar a nuestro señor el rey David, diciendo: ‘Haga vuestro Dios que el nombre de Salomón sea más ilustre que el vuestro, y su trono más grande que el vuestro’. Y el rey se ha inclinado en su lecho.
texts.1ki.1.48: Asimismo, el rey ha dicho: ‘Bendito sea Yahvé, Dios de Israel, que ha concedido hoy que uno se siente en mi trono, y que mis ojos lo vean’”.
texts.1ki.1.49: Entonces todos los invitados de Adonías se llenaron de pavor, y se levantaron y se fue cada uno por su camino.
texts.1ki.1.50: Adonías, temeroso de Salomón, se levantó y fue a asirse de los cuernos del altar.
texts.1ki.1.51: Informaron de ello a Salomón, diciendo: “He aquí que Adonías tiene miedo del rey Salomón, pues se ha asido de los cuernos del altar, diciendo: ‘Que el rey Salomón me jure hoy mismo que no matará a espada a su siervo’”.
texts.1ki.1.52: Salomón respondió: «Si se comporta como un hombre de bien, ni un solo cabello suyo caerá a tierra; pero si se halla maldad en él, morirá».
texts.1ki.1.53: El rey Salomón envió a que lo hicieran bajar del altar. Él vino y se postró ante el rey Salomón, y Salomón le dijo: «Vete a tu casa».
texts.1ki.2.1: Se acercaban los días de David para morir; y mandó a Salomón su hijo, diciendo:
texts.1ki.2.2: “Yo voy por el camino de toda la tierra; esfuérzate y muéstrate hombre.
texts.1ki.2.3: Guarda las ordenanzas de Yahvé tu Dios, andando en sus caminos y observando sus estatutos, sus mandamientos, sus decretos y sus testimonios, de la manera que está escrito en la ley de Moisés, para que prosperes en todo lo que hagas y en todo aquello que emprendas;
texts.1ki.2.4: a fin de que Yahvé confirme la promesa que me hizo, diciendo: «Si tus hijos guardaren su camino, andando delante de mí con verdad, de todo su corazón y de toda su alma, jamás te faltará —dijo— varón en el trono de Israel».
texts.1ki.2.5: “Bien sabes tú también lo que me hizo Joab hijo de Sarvia, y lo que hizo a los dos generales de los ejércitos de Israel, a Abner hijo de Ner y a Amasa hijo de Jeter, a los cuales mató, derramando en tiempo de paz sangre de guerra, manchando con sangre de guerra el talabarte que rodeaba su cintura y las sandalias de sus pies.
texts.1ki.2.6: Haz, pues, conforme a tu sabiduría; no permitas que sus canas desciendan al Seol en paz.
texts.1ki.2.7: Mas con los hijos de Barzilai galaadita mostrarás bondad, que sean de los que comen a tu mesa; porque ellos me acogieron así cuando yo huía de tu hermano Absalón.
texts.1ki.2.8: “También tienes contigo a Simei hijo de Gera, benjamita de Bahurim, el cual me maldijo con una maldición fidedigna el día que yo iba a Mahanaim. Pero él bajó a recibirme al Jordán, y yo le juré por Yahvé, diciendo: «No te mataré a espada».
texts.1ki.2.9: Mas ahora no lo dejes sin castigo, pues eres hombre sabio y sabes cómo debes tratarlo; harás que sus canas desciendan con sangre al Seol”.
texts.1ki.2.10: Y David durmió con sus padres, y fue sepultado en la ciudad de David.
texts.1ki.2.11: Los días que reinó David sobre Israel fueron cuarenta años: siete años reinó en Hebrón, y treinta y tres años reinó en Jerusalén.
texts.1ki.2.12: Y se sentó Salomón en el trono de David su padre, y su reino quedó firmemente consolidado.
texts.1ki.2.13: Entonces Adonías hijo de Haguit fue a ver a Betsabé, madre de Salomón. Ella le preguntó: «¿Vienes en paz?». Él respondió: «En paz».
texts.1ki.2.14: Y añadió: «Tengo algo que deciros». Ella dijo: «Hablad».
texts.1ki.2.15: Él dijo: «Vosotros sabéis que el reino era mío, y que todo Israel había puesto su mirada en mí para que yo reinara; mas el trono se ha invertido y ha pasado a mi hermano, porque de parte de Yahvé era suyo.
texts.1ki.2.16: Ahora os hago una petición; no me la deneguéis». Ella le dijo: «Decid».
texts.1ki.2.17: Él dijo: «Os ruego que habléis al rey Salomón (pues él no os lo negará), para que me dé a Abisag sunamita por mujer».
texts.1ki.2.18: Y Betsabé respondió: «Está bien; yo hablaré por ti al rey».
texts.1ki.2.19: Fue, pues, Betsabé al rey Salomón para hablarle por Adonías. El rey se levantó a recibirla y se inclinó ante ella; se sentó en su trono e hizo poner un trono para su madre, la cual se sentó a su diestra.
texts.1ki.2.20: Ella le dijo: «Una pequeña petición tengo que hacerte; no me la deniegues». El rey respondió: «Pedid, madre mía, que yo no os la denegaré».
texts.1ki.2.21: Y ella dijo: «Dese a Abisag sunamita por mujer a tu hermano Adonías».
texts.1ki.2.22: El rey Salomón respondió a su madre: «¿Por qué pides a Abisag sunamita para Adonías? Pide también para él el reino; pues él es mi hermano mayor, y tiene consigo al sacerdote Abiatar y a Joab hijo de Sarvia».
texts.1ki.2.23: Y el rey Salomón juró por Yahvé, diciendo: «Traiga Dios sobre mí el peor de los castigos si Adonías no ha pronunciado estas palabras contra su propia vida.
texts.1ki.2.24: Ahora, pues, vive Yahvé, que me ha confirmado y me ha sentado en el trono de mi padre David, y que me ha hecho casa, como había prometido, que Adonías morirá hoy mismo».
texts.1ki.2.25: Entonces el rey Salomón envió a Benaía hijo de Joyadá, el cual arremetió contra él, y murió.
texts.1ki.2.26: Y al sacerdote Abiatar dijo el rey: «Vete a Anatot, a tus campos, pues eres digno de muerte; mas no te mataré hoy, por cuanto has llevado el arca del Señor Yahvé delante de David mi padre, y has compartido todas las aflicciones de mi padre».
texts.1ki.2.27: Así echó Salomón a Abiatar del sacerdocio de Yahvé, para que se cumpliese la palabra que Yahvé había pronunciado en Silo sobre la casa de Elí.
texts.1ki.2.28: Llegó la noticia a Joab (porque Joab se había unido a Adonías, aunque no se había unido a Absalón); y huyó Joab al Tabernáculo de Yahvé y se asió de los cuernos del altar.
texts.1ki.2.29: Y se le comunicó a Salomón: «Joab ha huido al Tabernáculo de Yahvé, y he aquí que está junto al altar». Entonces envió Salomón a Benaía hijo de Joyadá, diciendo: «Ve y arremete contra él».
texts.1ki.2.30: Entró Benaía al Tabernáculo de Yahvé y le dijo: «El rey ha dicho que salgas». Él dijo: «No, sino que aquí moriré». Benaía volvió con la respuesta al rey, diciendo: «Así habló Joab, y así me respondió».
texts.1ki.2.31: El rey le dijo: «Haz como él ha dicho; mátale y entiérrale, y quita de mí y de la casa de mi padre la sangre que Joab derramó injustamente.
texts.1ki.2.32: Yahvé hará recaer la sangre de Joab sobre su propia cabeza; pues él arremetió contra dos hombres más justos y mejores que él, a los cuales mató a espada sin que mi padre David supiese nada: a Abner hijo de Ner, general del ejército de Israel, y a Amasa hijo de Jeter, general del ejército de Judá.
texts.1ki.2.33: La sangre de ellos recaerá sobre la cabeza de Joab y sobre la cabeza de su descendencia para siempre; mas sobre David, sobre su descendencia, sobre su casa y sobre su trono, habrá perpetuamente paz de parte de Yahvé».
texts.1ki.2.34: Entonces Benaía hijo de Joyadá subió, arremetió contra él y lo mató; y fue sepultado en su casa, en el desierto.
texts.1ki.2.35: El rey puso en su lugar a Benaía hijo de Joyadá al frente del ejército, y al sacerdote Sadoc puso el rey en lugar de Abiatar.
texts.1ki.2.36: Después envió el rey a llamar a Simei, y le dijo: «Edifícate una casa en Jerusalén y habita allí, y no salgas de allí a ninguna parte;
texts.1ki.2.37: porque sabe de cierto que el día que salieres y pasares el torrente de Cedrón, sin duda morirás, y tu sangre recaerá sobre tu cabeza».
texts.1ki.2.38: Simei dijo al rey: «La palabra es buena; como mi señor el rey ha dicho, así lo hará vuestro siervo». Y habitó Simei en Jerusalén muchos días.
texts.1ki.2.39: Pero pasados tres años, sucedió que dos esclavos de Simei huyeron a Aquis hijo de Maaca, rey de Gat. Y dieron aviso a Simei, diciendo: «Tus esclavos están en Gat».
texts.1ki.2.40: Entonces Simei se levantó, ensilló su asno y fue a Gat, a Aquis, para buscar a sus esclavos. Fue, pues, Simei, y trajo sus esclavos de Gat.
texts.1ki.2.41: Luego se le dijo a Salomón que Simei había ido de Jerusalén a Gat, y que había vuelto.
texts.1ki.2.42: El rey mandó llamar a Simei y le dijo: “¿No te hice jurar yo por Yahvé y te protesté diciendo: «Sabe de cierto que el día que salieres para ir a alguna otra parte, ciertamente morirás»?
texts.1ki.2.43: ¿Por qué, pues, no has guardado el juramento de Yahvé y el mandamiento que te impuse?”.
texts.1ki.2.44: Dijo además el rey a Simei: «Tú sabes en tu corazón todo el mal que hiciste a mi padre David; Yahvé, pues, ha hecho recaer tu maldad sobre tu propia cabeza.
texts.1ki.2.45: Y el rey Salomón será bendito, y el trono de David será firme perpetuamente delante de Yahvé».
texts.1ki.2.46: Entonces el rey mandó a Benaía hijo de Joyadá, el cual salió, arremetió contra él y murió. Y el reino fue confirmado en la mano de Salomón.
texts.1ki.3.1: Salomón emparentó con el faraón, rey de Egipto, pues tomó a la hija del faraón y la trajo a la ciudad de David, hasta que hubo acabado de edificar su propia casa, la casa de Yahvé y los muros alrededor de Jerusalén.
texts.1ki.3.2: Sin embargo, el pueblo sacrificaba todavía en los lugares altos, porque aún no se había edificado casa al nombre de Yahvé.
texts.1ki.3.3: Mas Salomón amaba a Yahvé, andando en los estatutos de su padre David; solamente sacrificaba y quemaba incienso en los lugares altos.
texts.1ki.3.4: E iba el rey a Gabaón para sacrificar allí, porque aquel era el lugar alto principal; mil holocaustos ofreció Salomón sobre aquel altar.
texts.1ki.3.5: Y se apareció Yahvé a Salomón en Gabaón una noche en sueños, y le dijo Dios: «Pedid lo que queráis que yo os dé».
texts.1ki.3.6: Y Salomón dijo: «Vos habéis hecho gran misericordia a vuestro siervo David mi padre, según él anduvo delante de vos en verdad, en justicia y en rectitud de corazón para con vos; y vos le habéis guardado esta vuestra gran misericordia, al darle un hijo que se sentase en su trono, como sucede hoy.
texts.1ki.3.7: Ahora pues, Yahvé Dios mío, vos habéis puesto a vuestro siervo por rey en lugar de David mi padre; y yo soy un joven pequeño, que no sé cómo entrar ni salir.
texts.1ki.3.8: Y vuestro siervo está en medio de vuestro pueblo al cual vos escogisteis; un pueblo tan grande que no se puede contar ni numerar por su multitud.
texts.1ki.3.9: Dad, pues, a vuestro siervo un corazón dócil para juzgar a vuestro pueblo, y para discernir entre el bien y el mal; porque ¿quién podrá gobernar este vuestro pueblo tan grande?».
texts.1ki.3.10: Y agradó esta petición delante del Señor, que Salomón hubiese pedido esto.
texts.1ki.3.11: Y le dijo Dios: «Porque habéis pedido esto, y no pedisteis para vos muchos días, ni pedisteis para vos riquezas, ni pedisteis la vida de vuestros enemigos, sino que demandasteis para vos inteligencia para oír juicio,
texts.1ki.3.12: he aquí lo he hecho conforme a vuestras palabras; he aquí que os he dado un corazón sabio y entendido, tanto que no ha habido antes de vos otro como vos, ni después de vos se levantará otro como vos.
texts.1ki.3.13: Y aun lo que no pedisteis os he dado, riquezas y gloria, de tal manera que entre los reyes ninguno haya como vos en todos vuestros días.
texts.1ki.3.14: Y si anduviereis en mis caminos, guardando mis estatutos y mis mandamientos, como anduvo vuestro padre David, yo alargaré vuestros días».
texts.1ki.3.15: Cuando Salomón despertó, vio que era sueño; y vino a Jerusalén, y se presentó delante del arca de la alianza de Yahvé, y sacrificó holocaustos y ofreció sacrificios de paz, e hizo también un banquete a todos sus siervos.
texts.1ki.3.16: En aquel tiempo vinieron al rey dos mujeres meretrices, y se presentaron delante de él.
texts.1ki.3.17: Y dijo una de ellas: «¡Ah, señor mío! Yo y esta mujer morábamos en una misma casa, y yo di a luz estando con ella en la casa.
texts.1ki.3.18: Sucedió al tercer día de mi alumbramiento, que esta dio a luz también, y estábamos nosotras juntas; ninguno de fuera estaba en casa, sino nosotras dos.
texts.1ki.3.19: Y el hijo de esta mujer murió de noche, porque ella se acostó sobre él.
texts.1ki.3.20: Y se levantó a medianoche y tomó a mi hijo de mi lado, estando vuestra sierva dormida, y lo puso a su lado, y puso al lado mío a su hijo muerto.
texts.1ki.3.21: Y cuando yo me levanté de madrugada para dar el pecho a mi hijo, he aquí que estaba muerto; pero lo observé por la mañana, y vi que no era mi hijo, el que yo había dado a luz».
texts.1ki.3.22: Entonces la otra mujer dijo: «No; mi hijo es el que vive, y tu hijo es el muerto». Y la otra volvió a decir: «No; tu hijo es el muerto, y mi hijo es el que vive». Así hablaban delante del rey.
texts.1ki.3.23: El rey entonces dijo: «Esta dice: «Mi hijo es el que vive, y tu hijo es el muerto»; y la otra dice: «No, sino que tu hijo es el muerto, y mi hijo es el que vive»».
texts.1ki.3.24: Y dijo el rey: «Traedme una espada». Y trajeron una espada delante del rey.
texts.1ki.3.25: En seguida el rey dijo: «Partid en dos al niño vivo, y dad la mitad a la una, y la otra mitad a la otra».
texts.1ki.3.26: Entonces la mujer de quien era el hijo vivo habló al rey (porque sus entrañas se conmovieron por su hijo), y dijo: «¡Ah, señor mío! Dad a esta el niño vivo, y no lo matéis». Mas la otra dijo: «Ni a mí ni a ti; partidlo».
texts.1ki.3.27: Entonces el rey respondió y dijo: «Dad a aquella el hijo vivo, y no lo matéis; ella es su madre».
texts.1ki.3.28: Y todo Israel oyó aquel juicio que había dado el rey; y temieron al rey, porque vieron que había en él sabiduría de Dios para juzgar.
texts.1ki.4.1: El rey Salomón, pues, fue rey sobre todo Israel.
texts.1ki.4.2: Y estos fueron los príncipes que tuvo: Azarías hijo de Sadoc, sacerdote;
texts.1ki.4.3: Elihoref y Ahías, hijos de Sisá, escribas; Josafat hijo de Ahilud, canciller;
texts.1ki.4.4: Benaía hijo de Joiada estaba al frente del ejército; Sadoc y Abiatar eran los sacerdotes;
texts.1ki.4.5: Azarías hijo de Natán estaba sobre los gobernadores; Zabud hijo de Natán era ministro principal, amigo del rey;
texts.1ki.4.6: Ahisar estaba al frente de la casa; y Adoniram hijo de Abda estaba sobre el tributo laboral.
texts.1ki.4.7: Tenía Salomón doce oficiales sobre todo Israel, los cuales abastecían al rey y a su casa. Cada uno de ellos suministraba provisiones un mes al año.
texts.1ki.4.8: Y estos son sus nombres: el hijo de Hur, en la región montañosa de Efraín;
texts.1ki.4.9: el hijo de Deker, en Macaz, en Saalbim, en Bet-semes y en Elón-bet-hanán;
texts.1ki.4.10: el hijo de Hesed, en Arubot; suyos eran Soco y toda la tierra de Hefer;
texts.1ki.4.11: el hijo de Abinadab, en toda la región de Dor; este tenía por mujer a Tafat, hija de Salomón;
texts.1ki.4.12: Baana hijo de Ahilud, en Taanac y Meguido, y en toda Bet-seán, que está al lado de Zaretán, abajo de Jezreel, desde Bet-seán hasta Abel-mejolá, hasta más allá de Jocmeam;
texts.1ki.4.13: el hijo de Geber, en Ramot de Galaad; suyas eran las aldeas de Jair hijo de Manasés, las cuales están en Galaad; suya era también la región de Argob, que está en Basán: sesenta grandes ciudades con muros y cerrojos de bronce;
texts.1ki.4.14: Ahinadab hijo de Iddo, en Mahanaim;
texts.1ki.4.15: Ahimaas, en Neftalí; este también tomó por mujer a Basemat, hija de Salomón;
texts.1ki.4.16: Baana hijo de Husai, en Aser y en Alot;
texts.1ki.4.17: Josafat hijo de Parúa, en Isacar;
texts.1ki.4.18: Simei hijo de Ela, en Benjamín;
texts.1ki.4.19: Geber hijo de Uri, en la tierra de Galaad, la tierra de Sehón, rey de los amorreos, y de Og, rey de Basán; este era el único oficial en aquella tierra.
texts.1ki.4.20: Judá e Israel eran tan numerosos como la arena que está junto al mar en multitud, y comían, bebían y se alegraban.
texts.1ki.4.21: Y Salomón señoreaba sobre todos los reinos desde el Río hasta la tierra de los filisteos y hasta la frontera de Egipto; y traían presentes y sirvieron a Salomón todos los días de su vida.
texts.1ki.4.22: La provisión de Salomón para cada día era de treinta coros de flor de harina y sesenta coros de harina,
texts.1ki.4.23: diez bueyes gordos, veinte bueyes de pasto y cien ovejas; sin contar los ciervos, gacelas, corzos y aves engordadas.
texts.1ki.4.24: Porque él dominaba en toda la región de este lado del Río, desde Tifsa hasta Gaza, sobre todos los reyes de este lado del Río; y tuvo paz por todos lados en derredor suyo.
texts.1ki.4.25: Y Judá e Israel vivieron seguros, cada uno debajo de su parra y debajo de su higuera, desde Dan hasta Beerseba, todos los días de Salomón.
texts.1ki.4.26: Tenía además Salomón cuarenta mil caballerizas de caballos para sus carros, y doce mil jinetes.
texts.1ki.4.27: Y aquellos oficiales abastecían al rey Salomón y a todos los que a la mesa del rey Salomón venían, cada uno en su mes; hacían que no faltase nada.
texts.1ki.4.28: Llevaban también la cebada y la paja para los caballos y para las bestias de carga al lugar donde estaba el rey, cada uno conforme al turno que le correspondía.
texts.1ki.4.29: Y dio Dios a Salomón sabiduría y prudencia muy grandes, y anchura de corazón como la arena que está a la orilla del mar.
texts.1ki.4.30: Era la sabiduría de Salomón mayor que la de todos los orientales, y mayor que toda la sabiduría de los egipcios.
texts.1ki.4.31: Aun fue más sabio que todos los hombres: más que Etán ezraíta, y que Hemán, Calcol y Darda, hijos de Mahol; y fue conocido entre todas las naciones de alrededor.
texts.1ki.4.32: Y compuso tres mil proverbios, y sus cantares fueron mil cinco.
texts.1ki.4.33: También disertó sobre los árboles, desde el cedro del Líbano hasta el hisopo que nace en la pared. Asimismo disertó sobre los animales, sobre las aves, sobre los reptiles y sobre los peces.
texts.1ki.4.34: Y para oír la sabiduría de Salomón venían de todos los pueblos y de parte de todos los reyes de la tierra, donde se había oído de su sabiduría.
texts.1ki.5.1: Hiram, rey de Tiro, envió a sus siervos a Salomón, tras oír que lo habían ungido por rey en lugar de su padre; porque Hiram siempre había amado a David.
texts.1ki.5.2: Salomón envió a decir a Hiram:
